subject: Performance-tied 2yr prepay proposal with quarterly true-up and mid-contract expansion option
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netlayer.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@netlayer.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 2-yr prepay with performance-linked true-up

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — NetLayer's product team is excited about Redwood's latency profile for our low-latency chat flows. We ran initial usage modeling and want to explore a 2-year committed prepay with two constraints:

- Quarterly true-ups (we expect ramp variability in year 1)
- Pricing tied to a simple performance SLA (p50 latency <= 120ms): if Redwood consistently meets SLA we want an additional incremental discount applied to the committed rate.

High level ask: a draft schedule showing committed spend cadence (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 for both years), target discount bands (by ARR bucket) and a concise definition of how the performance-linked uplift/penalty would be measured.

Attached: NetLayer_Forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx (high-level usage plan) — we can share more details under NDA if useful.

Can you propose a structure by end of day Monday? We are on a tight timeline for procurement.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Rao
Procurement Lead, NetLayer
priya.rao@netlayer.io

Attachment: NetLayer_Forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet with quarterly expected token counts and growth rates)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netlayer.io>, Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@netlayer.io>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 2-yr prepay with performance-linked true-up

Hi Priya — great to hear NetLayer moving quickly. High level we can support a 2-year prepaid structure with quarterly true-ups and a performance-linked uplift. Draft below, attaching a worked schedule (NetLayer_Prepay_Schedule_v3.xlsx) and a short SLA credit summary (SLA_Credit_Summary.pdf).

Proposal (draft):
- Commitment: 2-year term; commitment expressed as annual spend (floor) with quarterly allocated tranches (we can accept a floor of 60% of year 1 modeled usage to allow for conservative budgeting).
- Billing: prepayment invoiced annually in advance at the committed annual amount. Quarterly true-up and reconciliation (usage-based true-up against committed tokens; any under-usage is carried forward as credit for next quarter within the same year).
- Discount bands (by committed annual $):
  * Band A: $0-250k => 12% standard prepay discount
  * Band B: $250k-750k => 18% standard prepay discount
  * Band C: >$750k => 24% standard prepay discount
- Performance-linked uplift (applied on top of standard prepay discount if SLA met for at least 3 of 4 quarters in a rolling 4-quarter window): +4% effective additional discount. If SLA missed for >=2 quarters, we apply SLA credit (cash or bill credit) per SLA doc.
- Mid-contract expansion option: NetLayer can convert additional committed spend into prepay at the then-current Band discount rounded down to the next band; we can include a 90-day notice window for any conversion.
- Cancellation/true-up: standard true-up applies; early termination subjects to remaining prorated committed balance unless offset by consumption.

Operational notes:
- Measurement: p50 latency measured on production traces via our tracing hook (we can surface the latency dashboard to NetLayer monitoring).
- Auditability: Redwood will provide per-quarter token/latency reports and a signed summary for finance reconciliation.

Next steps: If this structure looks reasonable, we'll send an internal pricing approval request (Finance) and update the schedule with the numbers from your forecast. I included Karthik on the cc for pricing confirmation and Monica for commercial approval.

Attachments: NetLayer_Prepay_Schedule_v3.xlsx, SLA_Credit_Summary.pdf

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netlayer.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@netlayer.io>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 2-yr prepay with performance-linked true-up

Thanks Vivek — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

1) Mid-contract expansion: can you confirm whether an expansion conversion would use the effective discount at time of conversion or be priced off the original booking band? Ideally NetLayer wants the better of the two (i.e., if you move into a higher band we get that higher discount).

2) For the performance uplift, NetLayer would like a clear blackout policy (e.g., scheduled maintenance windows, force majeure). Also, can the SLA credit be applied as a dollar credit if the uplift is not met for the quarter?

3) We will need a clause allowing a one-time true-up to handle an acquisition-driven usage spike (example: we acquire a small app in Q3). Would Redwood consider a one-time elasticity carve-out (up to +30% of a quarter) without penalty if we provide 30 days notice?

Attached: a short internal forecast to help you slot numbers into the schedule. If we can get a revised schedule with explicit dollar amounts and the answers to the three bullets above by Wednesday EOD, our finance and legal teams can prioritize the review.

Best,
Priya

Attachment: NetLayer_Forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx (updated with acquisition scenario column)

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netlayer.io>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 2-yr prepay with performance-linked true-up

Hi Priya — thanks for the clarifying questions. Finance has reviewed and approved the following final positions; we can include these terms in the SOW/Order Form and proceed to DocuSign once NetLayer confirms: 

1) Mid-contract expansion: NetLayer will receive the better of (a) the discount band applicable at the time of conversion OR (b) the original booking band, whichever yields the lower net effective price for NetLayer. In practice, that means if the expansion pushes you into a higher band you will receive the higher band discount.

2) Performance uplift and blackout policy: blackout windows include scheduled maintenance >4 hours (pre-notified) and force majeure events. If SLA uplift conditions are not met for a quarter, Redwood will apply the SLA remedy as a dollar credit against the next invoice. If SLA is met for 3 of 4 quarters in a rolling window, the +4% uplift will be applied retroactively to the applicable quarter(s) as a credit. Details are in the attached SLA_Credit_Summary.pdf.

3) Acquisition spike carve-out: we will allow a one-time elasticity carve-out up to +30% of a single quarter with 30 days notice, capped at $150k incremental prepay conversion without penalty. Any additional expansion beyond that will follow the mid-contract expansion rules above.

Commercial summary (Finance-approved):
- Term: 24 months
- Committed annual prepay (example slots inserted based on your forecast): Year1: $1,100,000; Year2: $1,500,000 (escalator tied to agreed ramp)
- Effective standard discount: 18% (Band B based on Year1 commitment)
- Performance uplift: +4% if SLA met (max additional benefit 4%)
- Net effective discount if SLA met: 22%
- SLA credit: defined in PDF; applied as invoice credit.

Please confirm the numbers (we used the forecast you provided) and we will generate the Order Form + SOW. I have copied Karthik for the DocuSign routing; I can open the envelope once NetLayer confirms Acceptance in reply.

Best,
Monica Patel
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: NetLayer_Prepay_Schedule_v3.xlsx, SLA_Credit_Summary.pdf
